utterance:
Good news, Daniel: your examination shows normal leg strength, reflexes and sensation — so no sign of a pinched or slipped disc causing nerve damage. No fever, and no red flags. This looks like a mechanical strain of the muscles and joints in your lower back from lifting — a "non-specific" low back pain. I know it's very painful, but it usually settles within 2–6 weeks.

That's also why I don't think an MRI is the right move right a scan often shows incidental findings in healthy backs and would likely cost you money without changing treatment. Scans are for people with nerve problems, or if pain persists beyond ~6 weeks despite good treatment. If it hasn't improved in 4–6 weeks, I'll happily reassess and consider imaging then.

The best treatment is: keep moving as much as you can (walking is great), heat packs, gentle stretches, and avoiding long periods lying still — staying active is proven to speed recovery. Avoid heavy lifting and twisting for now, and when you do lift, bend the knees and keep the load close.

For pain relief: paracetamol regularly, and if it's safe for you (no stomach ulcers, kidney issues, or reflux), an anti-inflammatory like ibuprofen or naproxen. Note I'm avoiding tramadol because of your allergy. Is there anything else? Any history of stomach ulcers, reflux, kidney problems, or blood pressure issues? And does paracetamol or ibuprofen normally agree with you?
reply: I have never had ulcers, my kidneys are fine as far as I know, and paracetamol and ibuprofen agree with me completely. I just really thought a scan was the safest option so we could know for sure what is happening.

awards.label: Stomach ulcers or indigestion with anti-inflammatories
Kidney problems
Paracetamol as the analgesic

utterance:
That's completely understandable — scans feel reassuring. But without red flags, an MRI at this stage can actually mislead rather than reassure, and it doesn't change treatment for a simple strain. I'd rather avoid unnecessary radiation/costs and treat what's clearly there.

I've prescribed paracetamol (1 g, up to 4 times a day — maximum 4 g daily, never more) and ibuprofen 400 mg three times a day with food, for 5 days. Take them regularly while the pain is bad.

Safety netting: come back sooner if you develop new numbness or weakness in your legs, problems controlling your bladder or bowels, numbness around your backside, fever, or if the pain gets much worse. Otherwise, I'll review you in 4–6 weeks if it hasn't settled — and if it persists then, we'll talk about imaging and possibly physiotherapy. Does that sound okay? Any questions?
reply: I figured I would need an MRI to see what is going on, because honestly, I have been reading about slipped discs and people needing surgery.

utterance:
I get it — Dr Google can be scary! But surgery is only for people with significant nerve problems: leg weakness, foot drop, severe sciatica with numbness, or bladder/bowel issues. Your legs are completely normal on my exam, so you're nowhere near that territory. You have a good prognosis — most people with this pattern of pain recover well within weeks. If anything neurological does appear, that would be a different story and we'd investigate urgently — but nothing suggests that now.

So the plan: stay active, heat, the two medications, review in 4–6 weeks or sooner if red flags appear. Sound good?
reply: Alright, I understand. I will try to keep moving and take the medications, and I'll come back if anything gets worse.
